data.name: Cody Boyd
data.intro: Homelab-built, self-hosted, and ready to bring that hands-on discipline to a security team.
data.about: IT professional transitioning into cybersecurity, backed by a B.S. in Cybersecurity from Southern New Hampshire University, an NSA-designated Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense. Ten-plus years of customer-facing operations experience layered on top of hands-on networking, Active Directory, and endpoint management work from an IT internship, plus a self-managed homelab spanning Proxmox, Docker, and enterprise networking gear.

experiences.description: Contributed to the ECRS Catapult POS modernization rollout across 100+ Coborn's stores from the Retail Support Center in St. Cloud. Imaged and configured 4–20+ workstations per site via ManageEngine Endpoint Central, then coordinated palletizing and overnight shipment to stores. Wrote self-elevating PowerShell/batch scripts to automate Ingenico payment terminal COM port configuration via the registry, deployed from a network share. Rewired self-checkout lane light systems and configured LED Wiz controllers. Decommissioned legacy hardware with secure drive extraction/shredding and PIN pad destruction, and shadowed an onsite PCI compliance assessment. Used SolarWinds for monitoring and ticketing while working in Agile sprints.
Kept a 24/7 logistics operation running: managed freight exceptions, escalations, and delivery defects in Salesforce, and maintained the team's knowledge base.

Handled 20–40 customer interactions per day covering orders, returns, delivery, billing, and account inquiries, resolving on first contact where possible. Answered technical questions without escalation — sign-in issues, password resets, software activation, basic troubleshooting — routing hands-on repairs to Geek Squad.

data.education: B.S. in Cybersecurity, concentration in Networking & Network Security — Southern New Hampshire University (Online), graduated January 2026. SNHU is an NSA-designated Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense (CAE-CD). Coursework also includes Google's Cybersecurity Certificate: Foundations of Cybersecurity, Play It Safe: Manage Security Risks, Assets, Threats, and Vulnerabilities, and Tools of the Trade: Linux and SQL.
data.certs: CompTIA Tech+ (currently preparing for Security+). TestGorilla verified skills assessments: Active Directory, 90th percentile, and Cloud System Administration, 70th percentile (both valid through November 2027).

projects.title: Trapper Phil's
projects.description: Built and launched a site for an elderly veteran-owned wildlife control business to help him bring in more customers online. Also set up and optimized his Google Business Profile and implemented on-page SEO, improving local search visibility and rankings.

projects.title: Homelab
projects.description: A self-managed infrastructure lab spanning a clustered Proxmox VE environment, an Unraid media/app server, and a VPS. Runs 20+ self-hosted services behind Docker and Coolify, with Traefik reverse-proxying and automatic Let's Encrypt certificates, a Tailscale mesh VPN, and AdGuard Home for network-wide DNS filtering. This site itself runs on that same infrastructure.

projects.title: StockWatch
projects.description: A 3-tier SaaS restock & price-drop tracker — paste any product URL and it monitors the page (AI-assisted stock detection, or a manual CSS selector) and alerts you the instant something comes back in stock or hits your target price. Handles JS-heavy storefronts via headless browser rendering, not just simple HTTP scraping. Checks as often as every 5 minutes on paid plans, alerts via email, Discord, Telegram, push, or webhook. Built with a browser extension for one-click tracking, bcrypt + optional 2FA auth, SSRF-protected scraping, and seat-based Team billing for shared lists. Deployed via Coolify.

projects.title: PartsDesk
projects.description: A lightweight, self-hosted alternative for technical distributors and manufacturers to manage product catalogs — catalog search, an AI-powered assistant for product questions, and an internal knowledge base. Built with zero external dependencies: a Python 3 standard-library backend, a vanilla JS frontend, and SQLite, deployable via Docker.
